messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: correlated topic model code
parts:
Here's a version that actually compiles. I still haven't
actually tried out how well it works.

- Bob

// Blei & Lafferty Correlated Topic Model

data {
int<lower=2> K; // num topics
int<lower=2> V; // num words
int<lower=1> M; // num docs
int<lower=1> N; // total word instances
int<lower=1,upper=V> w[N]; // word n
int<lower=1,upper=M> doc[N]; // doc ID for word n
vector<lower=0>[V] beta; // word prior
}
parameters {
vector[K] mu; // topic mean
corr_matrix[K] Omega; // correlation matrix
vector<lower=0>[K] sigma; // scales
vector[K] eta[M]; // logit topic dist for doc m
simplex[V] phi[K]; // word dist for topic k
}
transformed parameters {
simplex[K] theta[M]; // simplex topic dist for doc m
cov_matrix[K] Sigma; // covariance matrix
for (m in 1:M)
theta[m] <- softmax(eta[m]);
for (m in 1:M) {
Sigma[m,m] <- sigma[m] * sigma[m] * Omega[m,m];
for (n in (m+1):M)
Sigma[m,n] <- sigma[m] * sigma[n] * Omega[m,n];
}
}
model {
// priors
for (k in 1:K)
phi[k] ~ dirichlet(beta);
mu ~ normal(0,5);
Omega ~ lkj_corr(2.0);
sigma ~ cauchy(0,5);
// topic distribution for docs
for (m in 1:M)
eta[m] ~ multi_normal(mu,Sigma);
// token probabilities
for (n in 1:N) {
real gamma[K];
for (k in 1:K)
gamma[k] <- log(theta[doc[n],k]) + log(phi[k,w[n]]);
lp__ <- lp__ + log_sum_exp(gamma); // likelihood
}

}

- Bob

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: correlated topic model code
parts:
I think you need to fill in the other triangle to pass the symmetry check at runtime, even if the other triangle is not actually used in the computation

for(m in 1:M) {
  Sigma[m,m] <- square(sigma[m]) * Omega[m,m];
  for(n in (m+1):M) {
Sigma[m,n] <- sigma[m] * sigma[n] * Omega[m,n];

Sigma[n,m] <- Sigma[m,n];
  }
}

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: correlated topic model code
parts:
The code you've attached uses a global covariance structure.
You could also fit covariance cluster-by cluster, so that
instead of

cov_matrix[D] Sigma; // covariance matrix

you'd have a covariance matrix for each cluster,

cov_matrix[D] Sigma[K]; // covariance matrix for cluster

The other thing to do is try to get a simpler model
working first. Does the output look OK with simpler
soft K-means?

You also have a much stronger prior on the means (normal(0,1))
than on the variances ([half] cauchy(0,5)). That should be OK for
this data, which looks fairly well behaved.

- Bob
